actions: Enumerated all 246729 FWER-feasible length-20 multisets over the 14 actions capable of beating the 1800-pair baseline and computed 79 distinct exchange-max power levels.

Proved a total first-order stochastic cost ordering for the 14 action-level conditional no-reject stopping distributions, Pareto-pruned to 1589 exact cost candidates, and certified the global optimistic q95 necessary envelope.
Resolved all 19 one/two-pair razor budgets with full-group checks and a power-constrained ordering DP; completed the exact integer-budget Pareto map from 1800 through 3300 with 29 breakpoints.

Derived a shared-uniform pathwise coupling proving fixed rho=.20 pair cost dominates arbitrary predictable history-varying rho_t>=.20 under sign-clock assumptions; stress-tested multiple adversarial predictable schedules with zero pathwise violations.

Separated the sharp failure mode where discordance retention depends on the current latent sign; a .60 vs .20 sign-dependent retention example changes observed sign probability from .50 to .75 and invalidates exact sign-tail FWER despite preserving the pair-cost lower-hazard bound.

Integrated exact within-candidate parallel batches b in {2,4,8,16,32} for the certified policies, showing candidate-stage fragmentation adds 7-10 q95 batch rounds beyond naive ceil(total_pairs/b) and q95 paid-pair occupancy rises roughly 0.3%-18.5%; three pair-count breakpoints become wall-round dominated for b>=16.

termination.cause: invocation response boundary after durable multi-stage checkpointing
termination.exact_next_action: Solve the wall-round objective directly: for b in {4,8,16,32}, jointly optimize action multiset and power-feasible ordering using exact batch-round CDF cost, identify any pair-count-suboptimal policies that wall-clock dominate the current evaluated frontier, then add variable rollout-time/straggler and asynchronous refill models.
